access_policy: Evaluation only. Open this file only after the persisted run is terminal and finished_at is set. It is not a RunConfig, Agent tool input, Shared State seed, or Jev input.

matching_policy.method: Deterministic post-run rules use assigned behavior IDs, actual verified assertions, acting identities/roles, scoped entity paths and sanitized API evidence. Ambiguous or unsupported records remain unmatched. No model, embedding or fuzzy matching.
matching_policy.deduplication: For recall count each scenario/bug_id at most once, even if create/edit inputs or multiple tasks expose the same bug. Keep the canonical confirmed finding mapping and duplicate records separately.
matching_policy.status_policy: Only CONFIRMED_BUG contributes to Bug Precision/Recall. Missing proof remains NEEDS_CONFIRMATION and does not silently count as detected. Preserve false reports and interrupted/failed runs.
matching_policy.unmatched_policy: An unmatched confirmed report is not a dataset match. Review credible unexpected behavior locally; if a reproducible in-scope defect is absent from these answers, flag a dataset validity issue rather than inventing an enabled bug.
matching_policy.controls: No-bug controls have zero expected defects. A correct control has completed checks and zero confirmed findings; no reports means Bug Precision and Recall are N/A for that run, not an invented 100%.

evaluation_rules.planning_success: Inspect TASK_CREATED/PLAN_CHANGE and final tasks. Every required_goal_id must be covered by executable checks with correct identity/data, scope, order and dependencies. Paired cases need at least three independent ready goal groups. Do not require predetermined task IDs or a pasted plan.
evaluation_rules.tester_task_success: Score explicit stable check IDs, their assigned identity, behavior and dependencies. All required checks must be completed and passed or linked to a correctly confirmed defect. Keep historical errors; successful retries or evidenced completion after recovery are recovered errors, while unresolved blocking errors fail the Task. Interrupted and never-started tasks are distinct. Runtime, report and formal metrics share the same deterministic scoring function.
evaluation_rules.end_to_end_success: All tasks and all explicit required checks must be correctly completed, including configured dependencies, every expected defect must have one evidenced canonical confirmed finding, controls must have none. Failed, interrupted and omitted work cannot pass. Completion text alone is insufficient.
evaluation_rules.bug_precision: Correct canonical confirmed findings / all canonical confirmed findings, with duplicates retained separately. Unmatched confirmed findings do not increase the numerator; use N/A for a zero denominator.
evaluation_rules.bug_recall: Unique matched enabled bug_ids / expected_bug_count. Count a repeated bug in each scenario independently. Use N/A for controls and never remove difficult or blocked enabled defects from the denominator.
evaluation_rules.reproduction_success: Successfully stably reproduced findings / findings attempted for reproduction, requiring two matches within three reset/fresh attempts. Independent verification is also required for confirmation; per-attempt reproduction success is a different supporting metric.
evaluation_rules.tester_metrics: Use LLM_CALL events with result.agent=tester grouped by task_id for requests/tokens/cost and JEV_CALL events grouped by task_id for Jev requests. Task latency uses TASK_STARTED and TASK_FINISHED or TESTER_FAILED, with terminal task.finished_at as a fallback. Count attempted tasks including failed/interrupted tasks, keep task latency distinct from summed LLM latency, and mark unavailable data explicitly.
evaluation_rules.parallelism: Only compare cases with expected_parallelism.compare_1_vs_3=true. Change both tester/browser-context capacity from 1 to 3, keeping scenario, switches, reset, data, model/provider, tracing and every other budget unchanged. Wall clock includes planning through final summary. Peak uses TASK_STARTED and TASK_FINISHED/TESTER_FAILED or terminal task.finished_at; utilization is active Tester time divided by capacity times the exploration window. Failed and interrupted intervals are not discarded.
evaluation_rules.resume_metrics: Design/static/local checks are not measured Baseline or resume results. Main planning/summary latencies and provider efficiency come from phase-tagged LLM_CALL events; judge plan and summary correctness only against completed-run evidence.
evaluation_rules.current_metric_gap: v2 uses shared deterministic check scoring; recovered errors do not permanently poison task success. Historical v1 runs have no explicit check IDs and are not directly comparable.
evaluation_rules.check_completion: Count unique correctly identified, ordered executed assertions / explicit required checks, including observed application assertion failures. Completion alone is not Task Success; unsupported deviations cannot pass. Duplicate assertions do not complete another check.

bugs.true_behavior: delete_task validates the target but does not remove it from stored tasks. The UI removes the row optimistically; reloading the task list restores it.
bugs.expected: A successfully deleted task stays absent in subsequent reads and after browser refresh.
bugs.actual: DELETE returns 200 and the row initially disappears, but the same task_id remains in storage and returns after GET/reload.
bugs.difference: Successful-looking deletion changes the immediate UI only, not persisted task data.
matching_evidence: Successful deletion action for the named task and project, with task_id or a unique task-title-to-id link.
Timestamped task list or DOM after refresh/reopen shows that same task still present.
Identity had authorized task access before deletion. A different task or a failed delete does not match.
bugs.trigger_context: Delete existing Seed Task in the joined seed project.

bugs.true_behavior: delete_project permits a member who has project access to delete a project owned by another user. The project and all its tasks are removed.
bugs.expected: A non-owner member deletion is rejected with 403 and preserves the project and tasks.
bugs.actual: An accessible non-owner project DELETE returns 200; the project disappears from refreshed lists and its tasks are removed.
bugs.difference: Membership or a retained access snapshot incorrectly grants an owner-only destructive operation.
matching_evidence: Acting username is a member and differs from the target project owner; membership/access relationship is established before the attempt.
Successful DELETE for that project and later absence of the same project in a refreshed list or owner-side read.
Owner or Admin deletion is legitimate and does not match. Denied attempts or hidden buttons alone do not match.
bugs.trigger_context: Act as the existing non-owner joined member against the seeded Admin-owned project.

bugs.true_behavior: create_project and update_project strip input but bypass rejection when the normalized name is empty.
bugs.expected: Create or Edit rejects an empty normalized name with 400/project name is required and leaves data unchanged.
bugs.actual: POST returns 201 or PATCH returns 200, and a project is stored with an empty name; refresh preserves the empty name.
bugs.difference: Required-name validation is missing on both creation and editing.
matching_evidence: Empty or whitespace-only submitted input established by configured data reference and recorded action.
Successful corresponding create/update and an empty project-name row linked to the same project_id after settling/refresh.
No validation message alone is insufficient. Different empty inputs on the same behavior deduplicate to this one bug.
bugs.trigger_context: Submit an empty string through Create Project; compare project row count before and after.

bugs.true_behavior: update_project persists the new name but returns a snapshot with the old name; the frontend copies that old response into the saved project row.
bugs.expected: Immediately after successful Save, the row and persisted reads both show the new name.
bugs.actual: PATCH succeeds and the dialog closes, yet the row still shows the old name. GET/refresh shows the newly saved name.
bugs.difference: Immediate UI/PATCH response disagrees with persisted data. The rename is saved, not lost.
matching_evidence: Old and submitted new names linked to one owned/Admin-editable project and a completed Save action.
DOM/screenshot of the old row name after the dialog closes and before navigation/reload.
Later DOM/read of the same project showing the new saved name. A genuinely unsaved rename or only post-refresh evidence does not match.
bugs.trigger_context: Rename the existing private project and observe the row before calling Projects or refreshing.

bugs.true_behavior: create_project ignores its submission-id deduplication lookup and allocates a fresh project for each request, even when requests use the same operation identifier.
bugs.expected: Repeating one create operation with the same nonempty submission_id returns the same project_id and creates one stored project.
bugs.actual: Two requests with the same nonempty submission_id return different project_ids and leave two separate projects with the same supplied name.
bugs.difference: Idempotence of one pending create operation is lost; separate completed create operations remain valid.
matching_evidence: Two create requests carry the SAME nonempty submission_id for the scoped input name and acting username; preserve sanitized request-body evidence or equivalent verified operation identity.
Two successful responses or refreshed rows show distinct project_ids for those same-operation requests.

Same names or two ordinary sequential clicks alone do not match: the first completed response rotates projectSubmissionId. Current NETWORK evidence stores method/URL/status only, and TRACE sanitization strips request bodies.
